stem: A child has chronic wet cough and is being assessed for protracted bacterial bronchitis; which additional feature would be least typical of protracted bacterial bronchitis alone?

options.text: Wet cough lasting more than 4 weeks
A normal or non-specific chest X-ray
Resolution after one or two antibiotic courses

explanation: Prominent concurrent wheeze is least typical of protracted bacterial bronchitis alone. Protracted bacterial bronchitis usually presents with a chronic wet cough lasting more than 4 weeks, with a normal or non-specific chest X-ray, and it often responds to one or two antibiotic courses.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because prominent concurrent wheeze is described as uncommon in protracted bacterial bronchitis alone.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a wet cough lasting more than 4 weeks is a key feature of protracted bacterial bronchitis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a normal or non-specific chest X-ray is typical in protracted bacterial bronchitis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because bronchoscopy is usually not needed in straightforward protracted bacterial bronchitis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because many cases resolve after one or two antibiotic courses.
